summary: Hybrid-capture 54-gene myeloid NGS panel on bone marrow aspirate reported as POSITIVE for clinically significant variants: NPM1 type A frameshift insertion (c.860_863dup, VAF 39%, Tier I), FLT3 internal tandem duplication in exon 14 (~36 bp, VAF 31%, ITD/WT allelic ratio 0.62, Tier I), and DNMT3A R882H missense (c.2645G>A, VAF 44%, Tier II). No reportable variant was detected in the listed selected genes including CEBPA, RUNX1, TP53, ASXL1, IDH1, IDH2, and others. The interpretation states that, in the context of an AML established by morphology and flow cytometry, mutated NPM1 is a WHO and ICC disease-defining abnormality and the diagnosis is therefore acute myeloid leukemia with mutated NPM1, with no 20% blast threshold required. FLT3-ITD is described as prognostically adverse and a therapeutic target; DNMT3A R882H is described as not by itself defining or changing the WHO/ICC category. Correlation with morphology, flow cytometry, and cytogenetics is recommended.
